test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 08 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Pipe P can fill (4)/(5) part of a tank in 28 hours and pipe Q can fill (2)/(3) part of the same tank in 42 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 7 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 14 hours.

Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time for P = 28 × 5/4 = 35 hours; Time for Q = 42 × 3/2 = 63 hours.

LCM(35, 63) = 315 units (Total Work).

Efficiency: P = 9, Q = 5.

Filled in 7 hours = (9 + 5) × 7 = 98 units.

R efficiency = 98 ÷ 14 = 7 units/hr (emptying).

Net efficiency (P+Q−R) = 9 + 5 − 7 = 7 units/hr.

Required time = 315 ÷ 7 = 45 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 45 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given: **

P fills 4/5 in 28 hrs, Q fills 2/3 in 42 hrs, R empties filled part in 14 hrs after 7 hrs.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time;

Efficiency of filling pipe is positive, emptying is negative.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Full time for P = 28 × (5 ÷ 4) = 35 hours

⇒ Full time for Q = 42 × (3 ÷ 2) = 63 hours

⇒ Let Total Work = LCM(35, 63) = 315 units

⇒ Work done by P and Q in 7 hours = 7 × (Efficiency of P + Efficiency of Q)

⇒ Work done = 7 × (9 + 5) = 98 units

⇒ Efficiency of R = Work ÷ Time = 98 ÷ 14 = 7 units/hr (negative work)

⇒ Time for R to empty full tank = 315 ÷ 7 = 45 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

Inlet pipes add to the volume (positive efficiency), while outlet pipes or leaks subtract from the volume (negative efficiency).

Net Work Done

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours (where y > x), net work in 1 hour = (1/x − 1/y). Time to fill = (x × y) ÷ (y − x).

Combined Efficiency

When multiple pipes operate, total efficiency is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies: Eₜₒₜₐₗ = E₁ + E₂ − Eₗₑₐₖ.
